purpose: Open work only: what is left, in what order, and the pre-registered acceptance test for each item. State, evidence ledger, venue metadata and closed gaps live in docs/audit/todo-history.md (sections 10-15).
objective: The framework must WIN on every model task: R1 (LineageFlow hmmscan hits), R2 (Kanzi RMSD), R3 (FlowMol3 fg_dev), R5a (2D FM W2), R5b (CIFAR FID), R5c (MNIST FID), R6 (LineageFlow scPerplexity/pLDDT), K1 (FlowMol3 pb_validity), K7 (LineageFlow novelty). A TIE is a loss. A LOSS is an open mechanism gap, not a boundary to be published. Every cell that is not a win today has a mechanism gap below whose acceptance test is that win.
win_definition: A cell wins only if BOTH hold. (1) POINT WIN: at the cell's canonical protocol (same checkpoint, same N, same seeds), the framework's metric is better with the paired 95% CI excluding 0 and clearing the cell's alpha. (2) FRONTIER DOMINANCE: over the NFE grid, the framework's (quality, NFE) curve lies at or below the baseline's at every grid point, and the framework's plateau is better than the baseline's plateau. (2) is the load-bearing one: flow-matching inference saturates with steps, so 'the baseline with more steps' is NOT a valid control and NOT a threat -- the baseline's ceiling is fixed by its own inference protocol. The framework's claim is that it raises that ceiling AND reaches a given quality at fewer NFE. Both halves are measured, not asserted.
frontier_protocol: Per model: baseline and framework on the SAME checkpoint, prior, seed policy and N, swept over NFE in {10, 25, 50, 100, 200} (extended upward until the baseline plateaus for two consecutive points). Report per-NFE paired deltas with CIs, the plateau estimate (mean of the last two grid points), and the dominance verdict. A cell whose baseline does not plateau on the grid has an unfinished ceiling measurement, not a win.
recording_policy: Observations-only: write audit docs + todo.json + raw artifacts. Frozen CLAIMS.md / CONSOLIDATED_RESULTS.md / paper-A-final.* / tnnls_submission/** stay untouched without explicit user authorization.
decision_rule: An experiment runs only if it can change a claim's STATUS or a metric's MAGNITUDE. More seeds, more draws or a larger N on an already-measured effect do not qualify: they buy confidence, not strength. When a cell is power-limited or negative, stop measuring and strengthen the adapter: study the domain (the upstream implementation, the metric's own definition, the field's validity rules), write the design hypothesis down, change the code, then make ONE pre-registered measurement. A tie is a loss and is treated as an open gap. Seed top-ups after a run are forbidden in every case; a cell's canonical seed set is fixed in its pre-registration before the first number exists.
research_protocol: 1) Read the upstream implementation of the state space being perturbed (channel geometry, latent geometry, embedding geometry) before proposing anything.
2) Read the metric's definition and the scorer, not just its name: what does it reward, and would it reward the change we are about to make for a trivial reason?
3) State the design hypothesis as a falsifiable sentence with the expected sign and rough size, in the audit doc, BEFORE touching code.
4) Change one mechanism at a time; keep the old arm runnable so the before/after is paired on the same seed and the same prior.
5) One confirmatory measurement at the cell's canonical N/NFE/seeds. No seed top-ups afterwards.

6) Never frame the control as 'the baseline with more steps'. Flow-matching inference saturates in the step count, so the baseline's ceiling is set by its own inference protocol; the correct control is the baseline at its plateau, and the claim to prove is (quality, NFE) frontier dominance plus a higher plateau.
gate_note: The pytest entry is the fast canonical subset. Full pytest is run per change: 15 known failures (3 stale eval stubs; 12 order-dependent test_paper_metrics cases). docs-vs-code verifies 3370 claims since the 2026-10-21 archive move.
q1_gate: The requirement is a win on every model task, judged by win_definition (point win AND frontier dominance). Current state: R1 wins single-seed but the gain is one Pfam family (GAP-69 -> GAP-79); R2 wins small at one seed; R3 is a near-miss at one seed; R5a ties; R5b and R5c-production lose; K1's metric is saturated; K7 is inverted. GAP-76 already removed the MNIST first-moment defect (mean DeltaFID +7.75% -> -3.34%, 6 W / 0 T / 6 R strict), so the MNIST residual is a contraction, not a location error; GAP-78's offline screen then showed the contraction (kappa) predicts the sign while the base's dispersion (rho) does not. Every non-winning cell therefore has a mechanism gap whose acceptance test is the win itself; none of them is closed by restating a boundary.

open_gaps.design_hypothesis: Profile-aware perturbation, in two variants that share one control: (a) position-wise noise scaled by (1 - conservation), using the same Pfam HMM that the metric scores against, so the restart explores surface positions and leaves catalytic motifs alone; (b) perturb the ESM-2 embedding only and keep the sequence identity, so the fold is preserved while the surface changes. Expected sign: hits rise above the init-only arm, and the two variants separate - if (a) wins, the metric rewards motif preservation; if (b) wins, it rewards fold retention.

(c) The D-004b result means the comparison arm is init-only, NOT the plain baseline - beating the baseline again proves nothing new. (d) Reading the profile HMM per position costs a pass over the MSA; budget it.

open_gaps.gap: The surviving explanation for the rho contraction is the law of total variance: the restart injects independent noise at t=m and integrates to t=1, so the endpoint is approximately E[x1|x_m] rather than a draw from p(x1), and conditional means are under-dispersed. This is argued, not measured (docs/audit/gap67-covariance-preservation.md section 6.3). Separately, Theorem 5's variance term bounds the DEVIATION from the corrected prior, which is a different object from the MARGINAL dispersion measured by rho; GAP-67 measured that the marginal does not respond to the blend's second moment at all, so the two are decoupled and any paper sentence that conflates them is wrong.
open_gaps.design_hypothesis: The contraction is monotone in the injected noise fraction (1-m) at fixed restart time t0, and vanishes as m -> 1. The current design ties t0 = 1 - beta, so m and t0 cannot be varied independently; a fixed-t0 override is required to test this.
open_gaps.research: (a) The override must be additive and default-off so every frozen digest and D.4 vector is unchanged. (b) m -> 1 is the 'do not restart' arm; the prediction that the contraction vanishes there is nearly tautological, so the informative part is the SHAPE between m=0.2 and m=0.9, not the endpoint. (c) Any restatement of Theorem 5 is a paper-surface change and is out of scope here -- flag only.

open_gaps.gap: The claim is that the framework raises the ceiling and the speed of inference on a frozen checkpoint. Nothing in the repo measures that: every cell is one matched-NFE point, and the only ladder (GAP-57) covers one model at three NFE points with no plateau estimate. The mechanism is now on record (docs/audit/mechanism-core-driver.md): the driver re-noises the endpoint to the path time t=m, re-integrates only [m,1], and does that R times on a fixed total NFE, so it changes the DISTRIBUTION the sampler produces rather than the accuracy of one pass. GAP-64 measured that the single-pass sampler is already converged at 3 steps on MNIST (11.1035 -> 11.0675 from NFE=3 to 100), so the baseline's plateau is a property of its distribution and NOT a compute limit -- which is exactly why 'the baseline with more steps' cannot be the control. Saturation is model-specific: MNIST is flat from NFE 5, but the CIFAR baseline is still descending at 100 (447.8713 -> 443.7343), so CIFAR is the cell where a speed win is actually available.
open_gaps.design_hypothesis: The baseline curve is flat in NFE because it is converged, so the framework's advantage appears as a LEVEL difference (a lower plateau) and as a shift of the curve leftwards (fewer NFE to the baseline's plateau quality), not as a steeper slope. Expected sign: pointwise delta <= 0 at every grid point; plateau delta < 0 with the CI excluding 0.
open_gaps.research: (a) Per-model NFE grid and saturation point: the grid must start low enough to show the baseline's plateau (MNIST: 3 steps already suffices) and must not stop before it; section 0.2a extends by doubling on the baseline arm alone when 200 is not enough. (b) The metric's own N-dependence (the FID small-N bias, gap57 section 7) so the frontier is measured at N >= 1000 only; below that the verdict is SCREEN_ONLY and win=False. (c) The speed half needs the curve, not a point: the NFE at which the framework first reaches the baseline's plateau quality.
open_gaps.acceptance: (1) One frontier artifact per model: per-NFE paired deltas with CIs, the plateau estimate, the dominance verdict per rung, the strict-gain rungs, the speed ratio, and the NFE-to-baseline-plateau number. (2) WIN requires weak dominance at EVERY rung (CI_low of the improvement >= -1%) AND (at least one rung with a strict gain, CI_low > 0, OR a speed ratio <= 0.5), at N >= 1000. A TIE is not a win. (3) A baseline that has not plateaued on the grid leaves the measurement INCOMPLETE; that is not a win and not a loss, and section 0.2a says how to extend. (4) The report must state, per model, that the baseline's flatness is convergence (with the measured numbers), not a compute limit.

The surviving observable is the realised contraction kappa = tr(Sigma_restart)/tr(Sigma_base): 0.5465 (WIN -13%), 0.6751 (WIN -4.3%), 0.8674 (LOSS +2.4%), 0.9527 (LOSS +1.2%) -- monotone and separating, reference-free, and with a causal reading (the R rounds average the model's own conditional noise; 1 - kappa IS the noise removed). open_gaps.gap: The six remaining strict losses are production (+1.0..1.2%) and w16e1_60k (+2.4..3.0%), all under the effect floor but all losses. The single-pass sampler is CONVERGED at 3 steps on this cell (GAP-64: 11.1035 -> 11.0675 from NFE=3 to 100), so there is no truncation error to recover and the restart's only channel is the output distribution. The original reading was that the residual loss is dispersion shrinkage, and that a gate on the base's rho would fire only where shrinkage helps. That reading is now measured false: rho is a side effect of the contraction, not its cause, and it predicts the wrong sign on w16e1_10k. A gate on kappa is the surviving design, but a gate can only SKIP the restart where kappa is near 1, and skipping returns the baseline exactly -- a zero delta, not a negative one. So no gate can give production/60k a strict gain; their best attainable outcome is weak dominance (delta 0), which the frontier definition accepts.
open_gaps.design_hypothesis: The restart averages the model's conditional noise at t=m, so a noisy checkpoint gains a lot and a converged one gains nothing -- that part holds (5k is -11.9..-15.4% for every beta in {0.3,0.5,0.7}, so the win is not a knob artefact). What does NOT hold is that an observable can select on it: both candidate observables (rho, kappa) order the checkpoints but neither survives a within-checkpoint manipulation. The remaining hypothesis is a plain parameter choice, not a gate: a smaller beta (0.3) may hold the two loss cells inside the +1% margin at N=1000 while keeping the 5k/10k strict gains, which would give R5c weak dominance everywhere plus strict gains -- a frontier win without any selector.
